feature: Ask never fails because a document is too big to describe
summary: A change to a big traced drawing (a Statue of Liberty of about 200 pieces) now plans and lands instead of showing the server's 'request exceeds the available context size' error. Ask describes a big drawing to its model in short, fits every request to the window before sending it, and says any model failure in one plain sentence.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no switch changed from its default. Walk: Scripts/playtest/ask-changes-a-big-traced-drawing-walk.json.

try.shotNote: Before this change, on the old build: the Agent group shows the server's raw error under the drawing.

try.do: Press Command K, type 'draw the Statue of Liberty' and press Return. Wait for its row.
Press Command K, type 'make her robe a darker green' and press Return.
Read the Agent group: a row 'Made her robe a darker green' with its switch on, no error.
Press Command Z once: the robe goes back, the drawing stays.
Compare the robe before and after in the second picture.
try.shotNote: An earlier run of the same walk: the model took the pale pieces, so highlights on the face and arm darkened too.

evaluate: Does a change to a big drawing come back in a time you would wait for (about 100 seconds here)?
Is the darker robe what you meant, or did too much of the statue change with it?
If Ask ever cannot read something at once, is 'That was too much for Ask to read at once. Try asking about one part.' clear enough?
rough: No mock covers this: it changes what Ask tells its model, not anything on screen except the error sentence.

A traced drawing's pieces are named by colour, so 'her robe' is reached through a colour group (Teal or Pale teal) and the face and arm shift with it; one run turned the pale highlights into flat dark patches. Folded into making-a-part-of-a-traced-drawing-smaller-shrink, whose checklist now asks for the robe alone.

Measured: the request went from 39,719 tokens (refused) to 15,012, under half of the smallest window. It still takes about 90 seconds to read, most of it the tools; first-answer speed is ask-s-first-answer-after-its-model-loads-comes-i.

This Mac (64 GB) now runs Ask's model with a 65,536 token window, 2.2 GB more memory than before; Macs under 48 GB keep 32,768. The bigger window alone was not a fix: reading the old 38,000 token request took 325 seconds.
